HIR: source structure with semantic identities

HIR is the high-level intermediate representation. It retains source-level structure for analysis, diagnostics, and readable source emission, while replacing resolved paths with semantic identities. It is neither the parsed syntax tree nor a control-flow graph, and the existence of a HIR value alone is not proof that analysis succeeded.

See the overview for the whole pipeline, MIR for the execution-shaped successor, and adding a target for a HIR consumer.

Ownership and lifecycle#

ResponsibilityPublic source
Nodes and neutral fact carriersradix-hir, especially nodes.rs.
Read-only/mutable traversalvisit.rs.
AST-to-HIR productionradix-semantic lowering, LowerRequest, lower, and LoweredProgram.
Types and definition handlesradix-types.
Analysis sequencingradix-semantic and pass registry.
Successful module carrierAnalyzedModule in the driver.
HIR source-emission viewCodegenAnalysis in codegen/input.rs.
MIR-lowering viewAnalyzedModuleApplicationView in analyzed_application.rs.

Collection and resolution establish definitions, scopes, and type references before HIR lowering. Lowering normalizes syntax, creates HIR identities, and returns both the semantic tree and presentation data. Typechecking then fills or validates type facts; subsequent passes establish flow, effect, shape, legality, and other facts. These operations may rewrite eligible HIR forms as well as populate tables. The semantic coordinator, not the node crate, owns this ordering.

Collection/resolution/lowering hard errors stop downstream analysis. Typecheck and later passes accumulate diagnostics. SemanticResult can contain partial state, and SemanticResult::success requires HIR, access facts, and no error severity diagnostic. driver::analyze_source additionally performs the driver's qualification/admission work before returning an AnalyzedModule. Do not take a recovered tree directly to a backend because it is traversable.

Inspection is a different lifecycle: hir_inspection_for_source_with_config in inspect.rs prepares collection/resolution and lowers, without running the full typecheck pipeline. That is the source of faber hir output. It is useful for normalization bugs, not a certificate that an expression has its final analyzed type.

Core tree shape#

The following are existing types in nodes.rs:

  • HirModule contains items, an optional executable entry block, entry annotations, optional entry argument binding, and async-entry posture. The entry is for one source module, not a package root. entry == None is a legitimate module shape, not an analysis failure.
  • HirItem / HirItemKind describe declarations and imports. Functions, parameters, fields, methods, variants, and locals carry definition identities appropriate to their roles.
  • HirBlock holds statements and an optional tail expression. A tail expression is not an extra statement that a consumer may evaluate twice.
  • HirStatement has a HirId, kind, and source span. HirStatementKind includes locals, expressions for effect, returns, break/continue, and other normalized statement forms.
  • HirExpression has a HirId, HirExpressionKind, optional TypeId, and span. Resolved paths use HirExpressionKind::Path(DefId). Calls, method calls, blocks, conditionals, patterns, optional operations, and conversions retain their distinct semantic structure rather than collapsing to strings.

An internal enum name need not match the source keyword in a reader's locale. Consumers dispatch on the representation and consult the interner/locale contracts where spelling is actually needed; they do not reparse emitted names.

Identity and companion-state invariants#

Handle or factMeaning and consumer obligation
DefIdNamed semantic definition, defined in radix-types and re-exported by radix-hir. Resolution supplies many IDs; lowering also creates synthetic bindings. Carry IDs instead of resolving a name again.
HirIdAnnotatable HIR node identity used by analyses and presentation. It is not a DefId and is not a persistent source-location key.
TypeIdReference into a particular TypeTable. It is semantic identity, not a byte layout, target type spelling, or portable cross-module number.
SymbolReference into the corresponding Interner. Never resolve a symbol with another module's interner simply because its numeric value is in range.
SpanSource byte range for diagnostics. Normalization should preserve the source construct that ought to receive an error, not an invented target-code position.
Optional expression typeBefore typecheck, None is expected. A consumer requiring a final type must diagnose a missing fact, not select an arbitrary backend type. Other optional fields have their own contracts.

Keep arenas and facts coherent. AnalyzedModule carries an AnalysisStamp and the HIR, resolver, arenas, presentation, library registry, function facts, resolved uses, qualified identities, provenance, shape obligations, and other metadata from that unit. Neither CodegenAnalysis nor the application view is permission to combine independently produced tables.

This does not assert that every optional field becomes Some on success. For example, a local's explicit annotation and a function's authored return annotation have different meanings from an expression's analyzed type. Follow the field contract and resolver/type tables rather than imposing a blanket “all options filled” rule.

Side tables are semantic input, not backend hints#

Examples of carried facts and their owners:

  • FunctionFactTable in function_facts.rs records function effect/capture/call facts.
  • ResolvedUseIndex in resolved_use.rs records definition/import uses without asking emitters to repeat resolution.
  • ShapeObligationTable in shape_obligations.rs retains runtime shape relations at checked boundaries.
  • LibraryRegistry in HIR nodes carries library import provenance and imported declaration metadata.
  • TensorEdgePolicyTable in tensor_edge_policy.rs carries resolved policy/provider facts.

The list is illustrative, not an alternative schema. The analyzed carrier's fields and the consumer traits are authoritative for required facts.

Semantic tree versus presentation#

HirPresentation is a serializable sidecar in nodes.rs, not a field on HirModule. It carries trivia ownership/attachments, source anchors, structural block and module ends, entry explicitness, and witnesses for selected authored forms that normalize to the same semantic shape.

This separation lets semantic passes remain trivia-blind while formatting and conversion preserve distinctions that cannot be recovered from the tree alone. For example, elige_expr_ids records expressions lowered from the switch form; structurally similar authored match forms must not be re-spelled as switch just because a backend recognizes the same tree shape. The Faber path in codegen dispatch passes HIR and presentation together to radix-hir-faber, with witness normalization in presentation_witness.rs.

A HIR rewrite must consider which IDs, spans, semantic tables, and presentation witnesses it preserves or invalidates. Updating only the executable shape can silently break formatting or analyzed-artifact round trips.

Traversal and rewriting#

HirVisitor and HirVisitorMut in visit.rs centralize the recursive shape. Override the narrowest hook and call the matching walker when the traversal should continue into children. Omitting that call deliberately cuts off the subtree. visit_def observes introduced definitions, including bindings that are not top-level items.

Walkers visit HIR children, not the contents of type arenas or interners. They provide traversal, not semantic validation. Read-only and mutable walkers should retain matching recursive coverage. A new variant or field must be reviewed in both, as well as in analyses and consumers that need the new fact.

Consumer boundaries and rejection#

Shared HIR dispatch accepts CodegenAnalysis, rejects recovery expressions via reject_hir_errors, applies shared feature/type/leaf gates, checks target availability, and invokes the selected leaf. A supported source construct can still be outside one backend's implemented subset. A named rejection is preferable to partial or incorrect output. The recovery variant HirExpressionKind::Error must not become target placeholder code.

MIR lowering requires the analyzed application view, not raw HIR alone. It copies semantic identity into MIR and returns explicit errors for missing types or unsupported forms. It does not repair a bad semantic analysis by inventing one.

FHIR stores analyzed-HIR artifacts. Driver assembly/loading bridges wire data to coherent analyzed carriers; the format crate owns schema and integrity checks. Serializable Rust nodes are not, by themselves, a versioning policy. Presentation and other schema changes must follow the format's checks.

Focused investigation#

  • Wrong normalization: compare parsed syntax with raw HIR inspection, then inspect the matching semantic-lowering module.
  • Missing or wrong analyzed type: inspect semantic typechecking and the unit's resolver/type arena; raw faber hir alone cannot answer this question.
  • Wrong source re-emission with correct execution: inspect presentation witnesses and the Faber emitter before changing semantic nodes.
  • Missing definition only after linking: inspect package identity and arena remapping, not textual name lookup inside the emitter.

Useful existing proof locations are HIR node tests, visitor tests, presentation tests, and analyzed compilation tests. These cover different boundaries; none alone proves every backend or package route. This chapter does not establish exhaustive HIR coverage for any target.
